name: Pregame.com

title: Pregame.com Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Pregame.com review, checked 20 Nov 2026: prices from $6 picks to $1,995 a year, pro streak lines checked against Pregame's own records, the Deadspin dispute.
dek: A Las Vegas marketplace founded by RJ Bell that sells picks from about 30 handicappers in one cart, at $6 to $30 a play or up to $1,995 for a year of one pro. It publishes a graded archive and season records for every pro, which is more than most sellers show. On 20 Nov 2026 those records showed five of the six pros we checked behind for the current season, while their sales lines named winning runs.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Pregame or any handicapper who sells on it. This page reports what we could check on 20 Nov 2026, including figures from Pregame's own record pages, and labels everything else.

short_answer: Pregame.com is a real, long running business. Its terms name the operator, Pregame, LLC of Las Vegas, with a street address and phone number, it lists a toll free line and a support email, and it shows a price for every package. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Pregame is a store, not one handicapper, so there is no single Pregame record. Each pro sells under his own name and advertises streaks he picks himself, such as "316-263-7 Last 587 Premium Plays" or "NFL (+181 UNITS) #1 PRO". Pregame also publishes a win and loss page for every pro. When we opened the "Current Season" view for six featured pros on 20 Nov 2026, five were behind in Pregame's own weighted dollars, from about $333 to $5,932 at its standard stakes, and only one was ahead, by $231.

A 2016 Deadspin analysis of Pregame's archive found that the picks sold from 2011 to May 2016 lost money overall. Pregame's founder disputed it and sued, a bankruptcy judge blocked most of the claim, and the case was later settled with Deadspin standing by its reporting.

Treat every Pregame pro as a seller with a marketing record. If you buy, buy short, open the pro's own win and loss page before paying, keep your own log, and judge a pro after a few hundred picks, not a hot week.

guarantee: Pregame does not offer a money back or profit guarantee on picks, and it says so on purpose. Its discount page calls "guaranteed picks" a "deceptive marketing ploy" and argues they cost more than its own picks when a handicapper wins. That argument is fair as far as it goes: a pick guarantee never covers the money you bet. The same page mentions a narrow "Money Back to Comeback" insurance offer and links a Bet Like a Pro profit program, but we found no current terms for either.

The one remedy we could read is "opposite side insurance". The FAQ says: "I bought plays from two cappers on the same game. They are taking opposite sides. Shoot us a message" and links a 2009 forum post. That post says if you buy two packages whose top rated plays are on opposite sides of the same game, Pregame will credit your account with what you spent on both. It applies only to the top play in each package, is paid as account credit, and you must email support to claim it.

We found no cash refund terms in the FAQ or the terms of service. The terms say the service is provided "AS IS" and that Pregame does not warrant that content is "ACCURATE, RELIABLE OR CORRECT". Flex Access says it "Rebills at $195 a month unless cancelled via email". Discounts are limited to one per purchase, and Bulk Dollars count as a discount.

claims_note: How we checked: every Pregame pro has a public win and loss page with filters for time (yesterday, last 7 days, last 30 days, current season), pick type and pick size. On 20 Nov 2026 we set it to Current Season and All Picks for six pros featured on the pros page and added up the sport rows ourselves. The dollar column is Pregame's own "$ (Weighted)" figure, which appears to stake $100 per star: a 3 star Essler winner shows +$300. Pregame does not define the start of its "current season"; it includes 2026 baseball and the current NBA and college football seasons. Totals: Essler 253-231-10, down $2,956; Nover 274-248-5, down $333; Gomes 401-393-17, down $808; Goodfella 288-229-7, down $4,944; Spartan 495-494-10, down $5,932; Shaker 205-186-12, up $231.

Win rates and money do not move together. Goodfella won 55.7% of his graded picks this season and still showed the second biggest loss, because his NFL parlays and teasers at bigger sizes lost. Win and loss counts alone say little; the price and the size of each play decide the result.

The streak lines are chosen by each pro and change often. Under each pro the page offers "more streaks", which means more lines the pro selected, not a full record. Some pros do post losing lines too: sleepyj showed "2026-27 CFB / 68-76 -36.41 Units" beside his winning golf line, which is more honest than most marketing in this business.
record: Watchdog search, 22 Nov 2026: we searched about 1.37 million captured public posts from X, Reddit, Covers, TheRX and other forums for Pregame.com plays that were posted or reposted before a game started. We found none, so there is no Watchdog graded sample for this seller yet.

What a buyer can verify independently: very little. We found no full log of Pregame picks kept by an outside party that we could open, and no regulator record. In 2015 Pregame announced that a forum member would track Steve Fezzik's Bet Like a Pro service as an "impartial third party", but that tracking lives in a thread on Pregame's own forum and we did not audit it.

What Pregame itself publishes: an "Every Pro Pick Ever" page that lists pro picks with a date and time, the pro, the pick, the final score, the odds, the size, win or loss, and the dollar result. On 20 Nov 2026 its date menu went back to 22 Oct 2026, about 30 days, and showed 33 graded picks for the previous day. Each profile shows the last 10 picks (Essler's last 10 were 7 wins and 3 losses, up $490 by our sum), best records chosen by size and sport, and a link to the win and loss page described above. This is more than most pick sellers show. But Pregame grades and stores all of it, the times shown appear to be game times rather than release times, and in a 2019 response the founder said picks enter the archive "soon after the game starts".

The archive has been tested once in public. On 23 Jun 2016 Deadspin published an analysis of Pregame's archive by two bettors who scraped it. It reported that picks sold from 1 Jan 2011 through May 2016 added up to a loss of nearly $310,000 by Pregame's own grading, that a buyer who had bought and played every pick would be down $1,359,432 once the cost of the picks is counted, and that 11 of 49 pros showed a profit. It also said three pros, including Stan Sharp, had been removed from the archive. Bell told Deadspin they were deleted because their inactive pages drew search traffic, and released their histories, which Deadspin said showed one up 28 units and the other two down a combined 179 units. By Deadspin's count the roster as a whole picked about 51.67% against the spread.

The legal fight: the Las Vegas Review Journal reported on 24 Jun 2017 that Bell sued Deadspin's owner and the writer for $10 million, represented by Charles Harder. On 13 Dec 2017 Jezebel reported that a bankruptcy judge ruled the claim over the original article could not proceed against Gizmodo Media Group, leaving a narrow opening and the suit against the writer. Deadspin's update says the parties later settled, that it links Bell's response as part of the settlement, and that it stands by its reporting. In that response Bell said Deadspin counted inactive pros, did not adjust for pros on opposite sides of the same game, and that most active pros were profitable. That data is now more than nine years old.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Pregame.com handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform beyond what Pregame's own pages show.
our_data.context: For scale: Pregame's founder has written that 55% winners is the best a professional can hope for over the long run, and the six pros we checked ranged from 50.1% to 55.7% this season. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Pregame spans 2009 to 2026 but is thin, and much of it is about individual pros rather than the store. A lot of the talk happens on Pregame's own forum, which the company hosts and moderates. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found about a dozen independent posts across ComplaintsBoard, TheRX, Sportsbook Review, Reddit and Pregame's own forum, from 2009 to 2026. The oldest set, from 2009 to 2011, repeats one pattern: buyers said they paid for a heavily promoted pro, lost, and then saw the pro boast on the forum while other usernames praised him; several alleged that one seller used many usernames and that critics were banned. A 2009 TheRX member alleged that one Pregame pro was invented by the company, which others disputed. A 2011 Sportsbook Review thread praised Pregame's free information and podcasts while calling many pros losing and the promotion dishonest. Recent posts are about single pros: a January 2026 thread on Pregame's own forum alleged Steve Fezzik lost 95 units for clients in 2025, and a 2025 Reddit comment said he had been in the red for two years. Positive posts praise the free content, the opposite side insurance and, in one 2011 comment, years of profit following one pro. No post includes a full log, and we could not verify any of the figures.

In a thread on Pregame's own forum, a member claimed Steve Fezzik "lost -95 Units for his clients in 2025". Fezzik replied that he won just under 260 units from 2020 to 2024. A day later another member argued no buyer won those units once fees and lines buyers could not get are counted. Neither side posted a full log, and we did not verify either figure.
When Pregame announced its opposite side insurance on its forum, several members praised it as customer friendly. The posts are old and sit on Pregame's own site.

ComplaintsBoard shows a 2009 complaint, marked resolved, from a buyer who said the picks they bought twice lost while the handicappers claimed wins on the forum the next day, and another alleging that a seller promoted himself under several usernames and that critics were banned. In September 2009 a buyer said they paid for a week of one promoted pro and had six losing days out of seven. An October 2011 comment alleged the same pro had lost over 100 units for clients that year. These are unverified and more than 14 years old.

On the same ComplaintsBoard page, a commenter wrote in February 2011 that following that pro for years had been the best time of their betting life, and another in July 2010 argued that Pregame's own win and loss tool would expose any false claim. A long July 2010 reply defending Pregame's approach to losing streaks reads like a company response, though it is not signed as one.

A TheRX member alleged, citing someone who had worked at Pregame, that one featured pro was a fictional person created to sell picks. Other members disputed it and posted his monitored record of about 57% over 674 plays; one said that even if the name was a brand, the record was what mattered. Deadspin later reported that this pro's picks had been removed from Pregame's archive, which Bell said was done for search traffic reasons. We could not verify who he was.

A long TheRX post, also copied to ComplaintsBoard, alleged that a Pregame pro posted praise for himself under many usernames from 2007 onward. Replies included a member who said they would no longer send that pro their football money and another who said critics on Pregame's forum were banned for questioning records. These are allegations we could not verify.

In a Sportsbook Review thread, members said Pregame had many losing handicappers but useful free information, radio and podcasts. One past buyer said they could never post on the Pregame forums, their emails asking why went unanswered, and so they stopped buying.

On Pregame's own forum, a member alleged that Steve Fezzik sent paying clients the Rams +3 while saying on a podcast that the 49ers were the right side, and cited a 2024 paid NFL record of 62-58-2 without a source. Another member called him irrelevant apart from a short streak. We could not check either claim.

In an r/sportsbook thread about paying for picks, a commenter who said they bet full time told readers never to pay for picks and wrote that two well known sellers, one of them Fezzik, had been in the red for their services for the last two years. No figures were posted.

Trustpilot showed an unclaimed Pregame.com profile with 0 reviews when we checked on 7 Nov 2026 and refused our request today. The Apple App Store app named PreGame is an unrelated party game from another developer. Our Reddit archive check found Pregame mostly cited as a line source, not reviewed as a pick seller, and we did not find a Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to pregame.com.

conflicts: Pregame sells the picks, grades them, keeps the archive, writes the season records and runs the forum where buyers discuss them. That does not make the records wrong, but no outside party checks them.

We found no sportsbook links or promo codes on the Pregame pages we opened on 20 Nov 2026, and its affiliate page says "Pregame does not have a Affiliate Program." In his 2019 response Bell wrote that Pregame does not advertise or receive revenue from any sportsbook. Deadspin's 2016 story reported that Pregame sent customers to sportsbook referral sites, and Bell denied running them. We could not confirm either side for today.

Steve Fezzik announced on 1 Apr 2026 that he was leaving Pregame, yet on 20 Nov 2026 his name was still in the pros menu and his profile still carried his sales claims. A buyer could mistake an old profile for a current offer.
strengths: A named operator with a street address, a toll free phone line, a support email and a posted price for every package.

A public graded archive of recent pro picks with odds, size and results, plus a win and loss page for every pro that shows losing seasons as well as winning ones. Most pick sellers show nothing like it.
Some streak lines check out against Pregame's own records: André Gomes's NBA line matched exactly, and Stephen Nover's NFL line was close.
It does not sell "guaranteed" picks, and it explains why a guarantee does not protect a bettor's stake. Free picks, podcasts and a $25 join credit let you sample before paying.
Flexible buying: single plays from $6, weekend passes and a monthly plan that can switch pros twice a month.
concerns: Pregame's own Current Season pages showed five of the six featured pros we checked behind on 20 Nov 2026, while their sales lines named winning runs and "#1 PRO" claims.
The archive, the season pages and every streak line come from the seller. The archive menu reaches back only about 30 days, and the season view does not say when the season starts.
No refund terms found. The only remedy we read is store credit when two bought top plays land on opposite sides.
Deadspin's 2016 analysis of Pregame's own data found the picks sold from 2011 to May 2016 lost money overall. Pregame disputed it, and the lawsuit was settled with Deadspin standing by its story.
Heavy discount marketing, such as prices shown against $3,000 or $5,000 and "Price Will NEVER Be This Low Again", and a monthly plan that rebills until you cancel by email.
Old and recent buyer posts allege sock puppet praise and banned critics on the company forum. These are unverified, but they recur from 2009 to 2011.
checklist: Before buying any pro, open his win and loss page on Pregame, set it to Current Season and All Picks, and add up the dollar column across sports.
Compare the streak line on the package with that page. A run that starts on a chosen date is not a record.
Count units and dollars, not wins. Goodfella won 55.7% of his graded picks this season and still showed a loss of $4,944.
If you take Flex Access, put a reminder in your calendar: it rebills at $195 a month until you cancel by email.
If two pros you bought land on opposite sides, email support the same day to claim the opposite side credit.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business, Pregame, LLC of Las Vegas, with published prices, a support line and roughly 30 named pros, and it publishes more of its pros' results than most pick sellers. Whether those pros win over time is a separate question: on its own season pages five of the six featured pros we checked were behind on 20 Nov 2026.

Pregame, LLC, a Nevada company. Its founder is RJ Bell, whose real name the Las Vegas Review Journal reported as Randall James Busack; the terms list Randall Busack as the company's agent at 5860 S. Pecos Rd., Las Vegas. Bell has been an oddsmaker for the Associated Press and a sports radio host, according to Pregame's About page.

On 20 Nov 2026 single plays cost $6 to $30. Dave Essler's packages ran $89 for a weekend, $119 for 7 days, $249 for 30 days, $449 for 90 days and $1,995 for a year, and Flex Access cost $195 a month and rebills until cancelled.
Does Pregame.com offer refunds or a guarantee?
No cash refunds or profit guarantees that we could find. The only remedy is account credit if you buy two packages whose top plays are on opposite sides of the same game, claimed by email.
Does Pregame.com have a verified record?

Not an independent one. Pregame publishes a graded archive and season records for every pro, which you can use, but it keeps them itself, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to any Pregame pro. The only outside test, Deadspin in 2016, found the picks lost money overall from 2011 to May 2016.

For the money you get a pro's picks and analysis, plus public record pages you can use to check him, which most sellers do not offer. On those pages this season most featured pros were not beating the market, and there is no refund if the picks lose. If you buy, buy short and check the pro's season page first.
